# shellshare

> Live, read-only terminal broadcasting via a web link. One command, no signup.

Site: https://shellshare.net

## Install

`npx -y shellshare` (needs Node.js), or download the static binary then run
`chmod +x shellshare && ./shellshare`:
https://get.shellshare.net/?os=linux  (also: mac, mac-arm, windows; auto-detected from the User-Agent if omitted)

## Broadcast your terminal

`shellshare exec --json -- <cmd>` runs one command in a PTY, broadcasts it,
and exits with the command's exit code. With `--json`, stdout is
newline-delimited JSON:

- First line: `{"event":"sharing","room":"<room>","server":"https://shellshare.net","url":"https://shellshare.net/r/<room>"}` — parse `url` to get the share link.
- Last line: `{"event":"end","exit_code":N}`.
- Errors: `ERROR: ...` on stderr, non-zero exit.
- The link outlives the command: the room and its recent history stay on the
  server until it goes idle (6h), so a short command still leaves a viewable
  link, and the room name stays claimed by you for that window. Rerunning the
  same room name clears the previous run. (`shellshare serve` hosts
  the server in-process, so its link does die with the command.)

    shellshare exec --json -- npm test       # share one command
    tail -f build.log | shellshare --json    # stream a pipe (non-TTY stdin auto-detected, reads to EOF)

Output is end-to-end encrypted by default; the key is the 64 hex chars after
`#` in the `url` (a URL fragment the server never sees).

## Read someone's broadcast (no CLI needed)

Given a link `.../r/<room>#<key>`:

- Snapshot (history): `GET /r/<room>.bin` → ciphertext bytes.
- Live: WebSocket `/ws/v/r/<room>` → binary frames are ciphertext records;
  text frames are control JSON (ignore them).

Use one or the other, not both in sequence: a WebSocket connect replays the
room's history before its live frames, so the socket alone gives you both —
fetching `.bin` first and then following duplicates the history. Every
reconnect replays from the start too (that is what makes a dropped
connection a resync instead of a gap), so treat a reconnect as "discard what
I have and start over", never as a continuation. The `usersCount` control
frame is the last of the replay, so it marks where live output begins.

Both are a stream of self-delimiting records:
`[u32 BE N][12-byte nonce][ciphertext || 16-byte GCM tag]`, where
`N = 12 + len(ciphertext || tag)`, AES-256-GCM, key = the 64 hex chars after `#`.
(A link with no `#key` is probably a `--disable-encryption` broadcast — raw
terminal output, no record framing — but it may equally be a link that lost its
fragment in transit. The `size` control frame's `encrypted` flag tells them
apart; do not assume ciphertext is terminal output.)

The reader below does all of that. Save it as `agent.mjs` and run it:

    node agent.mjs '<url>'            # the history so far, then exit
    node agent.mjs '<url>' --follow   # history, then live until it ends
                                      # (--follow needs Node >= 22)

It writes plain text on stdout and leaves the rest to your shell:

    timeout 60 node agent.mjs '<url>' --follow          # bound the wait
    node agent.mjs '<url>' --follow | grep -m1 'DONE'   # wait for a marker
    node agent.mjs '<url>' | tail -40                   # just the tail

`--follow` ends by itself when the broadcaster leaves, which is usually
what you were waiting for. It cannot notice a closed pipe until it next
writes, so pair `grep` with `timeout` when output may stop first. Exit 0
on success, 1 on a usage error, an unreachable server, or a key that
does not match the room.

```js
{{AGENT_DECODER}}
```

Source: https://github.com/vitorbaptista/shellshare
